did_you_know.text: Did you know? Although the Torah mentions forty lashes, the Sages set the number at thirty-nine, so the limit would not be exceeded by mistake.
Did you know? Threshing is the process of separating grain from its stalks, sometimes by having animals tread on it. This prohibition protects the working animal.
Did you know? Levirate marriage is also known from ancient Near Eastern laws, such as the Hittite laws. It helped preserve the deceased brother’s family line and status.
Did you know? The ceremony described here later became known as chalitzah, from the Hebrew root meaning “to remove” or “to release.” The shoe became its central symbol.
Did you know? An ephah was an ancient measure of volume, mainly used for grain and other dry goods. Keeping two different measures allowed a merchant to cheat when buying and selling.
Did you know? The verb “vayezanev” is related to the word “tail” and describes attacking the rear of a group. That is usually where the slowest and most vulnerable people are.
